title: Native MD focus-tree structure review for the Greece 1970 regime paths
scope: Read-only audit of the requested Workshop MD generic and Russia focus trees, with the final Greece regime branch checked against those patterns. No runtime focus-tree changes.

native_semantics.prerequisite_blocks: Multiple prerequisite blocks on one focus are conjunctive (AND).
native_semantics.alternatives_within_one_block: Multiple focus entries in one prerequisite block are alternatives (OR).
native_semantics.positioning: Resolve x/y through relative_position_id before checking spacing or collisions.
native_semantics.mutual_exclusion: Use explicit mutually_exclusive links for selectable alternatives; later exit routes can remain available as separate focuses.

references.role: Primary reference: requested main MD generic focus tree.

examples.evidence: Relative position (-3,2) from GENERIC_political_reform (L142-L149); requires both cabinet reform and strengthen government in separate blocks (L148-L149), then upgrades the political-power idea (L153-L158). Good example of a meaningful AND gate.

Two separate prerequisite blocks require both public-service announcement and establishment (L232-L233), then grants a timed state idea (L237-L240). Shows a shared continuation after two complementary branches.
A political anti-corruption focus is offset at (8,1) from the reform root (L538-L544), costs 10 points (L542), and has a direct corruption-reduction reward (L548-L551).

A lateral exclusive fork under anti-corruption: decentralization at (9,2) and centralization at (7,2) relative to the same root (L607-L614,L644-L651). Both require anti-corruption and explicitly exclude the other. Rewards differ: decentralization adds a distinct idea and has agrarian effects (L618-L629); centralization adds its own idea (L655-L658).
Separate blocks require both diplomatic positions and our place (L673-L674), followed by a connecting political focus. This is a concrete AND convergence before a later fork.

Five outcome lanes share the station-in-the-world gate and use explicit mutual exclusions against the other alignments (L687-L700,L733-L746,L783-L796,L814-L827,L854-L874). Root spacing of roughly 2-3 x units illustrates broad radial political forks; consequences and availability differ by route.

references.role: Primary Russia branch reference from the same Workshop installation.

examples.evidence: Yeltsin anchor at (62,0), cost 1 (L52-L60). Subjects and Putin both depend on it, at relative x=0 and x=13,y=1 (L81-L93,L108-L122); Putin additionally requires actual reactionaries in office (L122). Demonstrates separated successors and a political gate.

Three alternatives at x=3,-1,1,y=7 from Putin (L553-L558,L601-L606,L649-L656). Each requires two distinct completed focuses in separate blocks (L562-L563,L610-L611,L659-L660), and excludes the other two (L564-L565,L612-L613,L661-L664). Availability distinguishes the political/economic outcomes; rewards diverge into centralization (L580-L590), corruption and oligarch influence (L628-L640), or a mixed verdict (L668-L676 onward).

references.role: Supplemental scenario-era tree in this mod, not the main-tree benchmark.

examples.evidence: Three sibling cabinet options around the government root at x=-2,0,2 (L152-L159,L181-L188,L216-L223), each pairwise exclusive and each with a different reward (L162-L170,L191-L200,L226-L232).

Two political directions share an OR prerequisite block and exclude one another (L405-L406,L437-L438); the later state focus requires professional civil service AND either political outcome through two blocks (L600-L601).
Two exclusive outcomes under the developmental strongman gate (L955-L956,L990-L991), with separate policy rewards (L959-L969,L994-L1002).

recommendations: Keep one common opening followed by three clearly separated, pairwise-exclusive regime roots at x=30,42,54,y=8.

Show distinct consequences directly under the roots: keep military rule, negotiate a supervised opening, or transfer power to civilians. A civilian cabinet must not be described as a genuine election or a completed handover.
Place the officer/service and security alternatives under the military compact. Keep the actual military exit funded and time-limited; a timer ending should not itself transfer power.

Let the supervised path split between retaining the military veto and negotiating it away. The direct-transition and two negotiated-exit routes can converge at civilian institutions through one OR block; use separate blocks for conditions that all must be met.
Represent replacement effects and retained legacies explicitly, including European censure and politicised officers where applicable. Distinguish permanent exclusions from revisable policy posture.

Maintain 6-unit or wider sibling spacing for descendant forks and run collision checks on resolved world positions. The final renderer now detours the tutelary-charter to reverse-opening edge around the tourism focus.
review_outcome: The final Greece graph follows the native fork and convergence patterns: three mutually-exclusive regime choices, route-specific package consequences, separately costed exits, and later civilian convergence. QA measured zero card overlaps and zero prerequisite edges crossing unrelated cards.
